correctness.rationale: Every step was reconstructed from the graph definition. Degree \(n-1\) converts the defensive condition to the exact threshold \(q=\lfloor(n-1)/2\rfloor\). The four index types produce the complete local-degree table, yielding necessary and sufficient inequalities. Domination and connectivity are proved separately, including the small \(n=3,4\) boundary. Multinomial counting then gives the full enumerator and minimum multiplicity. The embedded verifier directly enumerates all subsets for \(3\le n\le9\) and agrees with the theorem; those experiments are not used as the infinite proof.

value.rationale: The claim is a natural perturbation theorem for the complete bipartite family explicitly treated in the foundational paper. It identifies a sharp parity effect under deleting a perfect matching, proves a non-obvious automatic-globality and connectedness phenomenon, classifies every feasible set by matching-index states, and counts all cardinalities. These are structurally useful facts rather than a recomputation of a known scalar.
